prompt: You come round a bend and find temporary signs set up beside the road. What are they telling you?
options: That the road has been permanently changed and these signs will stay there for good
That the road ahead is closed and you must turn around
That conditions on this stretch are not normal right now, so what you would usually expect may not apply
explanation: Temporary signs go up for a temporary condition. The message is simply that things here are not normal today. Drive to what the signs in front of you say, not to what you remember about this road.
source_citation: NRTR 2000 reg 287(2); SARTSM Vol 2 Ch 3 §3.5.1 (message inferred from temporary signs)

prompt: A temporary sign and a permanent sign at the same spot tell you two different things. Which one must you obey?
options: The temporary sign, because it takes precedence over the other sign
The permanent sign, because it is the fixed, officially installed one
Whichever of the two you saw first
explanation: Most learners assume the bolted-down sign wins. It does not. Where two signs conflict, the temporary one takes precedence, because it is there for a condition that exists on the road today.

prompt: The permanent sign on this road sets the limit at 80, but a temporary sign at the roadworks says 40. What may you drive?
options: 80, because a temporary sign is only a suggestion
40, because the temporary sign overrides the permanent one
80, unless you can actually see workers on the site
explanation: 40. Where a temporary sign conflicts with a permanent one, the temporary sign wins — the bolted-down sign does not outrank it just because it is permanent.

prompt: A temporary Stop sign has been put up while a junction is being rebuilt. What does that sign look like?
options: A yellow octagon reading STOP, because temporary signs are yellow
A yellow triangle with a red border and the word STOP inside it
A red octagon reading STOP, exactly the same shape and colour as any other Stop sign
explanation: "All temporary signs are yellow" is the trap. Control signs — Stop and Yield — keep their normal shape and colour whether they are temporary or permanent, so a temporary Stop is still a red octagon.
source_citation: SARTSM Vol 1 Ch 2 (permanent and temporary control signs retain the same shapes and colours)

prompt: Apart from roadworks, where else will you meet temporary road signs?
options: At accident scenes, where traffic signals are out of order, and controlling traffic at schools and sporting events
Nowhere else, because roadworks are the only lawful use for them
Only on freeways and national roads, where traffic is fastest
explanation: Roadworks are the most common use, not the only one. The manual lists accident scenes, traffic signals out of order, and traffic control at schools and sporting events as non-roadworks uses of temporary signs.

prompt: How long may a temporary road sign stay up?
options: No longer than 24 hours, after which it must be taken down
Anything from a few minutes to several months, for as long as the temporary condition lasts
Up to 14 days, after which it counts as a permanent sign
explanation: There is no fixed lifespan: a temporary sign may be used only for a temporary condition. The manual records temporary regulatory signs standing anywhere from a matter of minutes to periods running into months.
source_citation: NRTR 2000 reg 287(2) (a temporary road sign shall only be used for a temporary condition); SARTSM Vol 1 Ch 2 (temporary REGULATORY signs may be used for short periods of time — a matter of minutes — or for relatively long periods running into months)

prompt: A temporary warning sign carries the same symbol as the permanent warning sign for that hazard. What is different about it?
options: The border changes from red to yellow and the triangle points downward
Nothing changes, because a temporary warning sign is identical to the permanent one
The background is yellow, while the symbol and the red triangular border stay the same
explanation: The symbol and the red triangle stay the same; the white background turns yellow. Treat that yellow as a prompt to slow down and expect something that is not normally there.
source_citation: SARTSM Vol 1 Ch 3 (all TEMPORARY advance warning signs shall consist of a black symbol on a yellow background with a red triangular border); NRTR 2000 Sch 1 — permanent warning signs, e.g. W306: Triangle red retro-reflective, Symbol black semi-matt, Background WHITE retro-reflective
